newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Canada's Bre-X finds Busang partner in Freeport.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Bre-X finds Busang partner in Freeport.

text.p: Canada's small Bre-X Minerals Ltd mining company said on Monday it had teamed up with U.S. giant Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc to develop one of the world's richest gold finds on Indonesia's Borneo island.
Bre-X chief executive officer David Walsh said in a statement his company would have a 45-percent stake in the Busang find, Indonesian interests 40 percent and Freeport 15 percent.

Freeport McMoRan, which has run one of the world's biggest copper and gold mines in Indonesia's Irian Jaya province through PT Freeport Indonesia for the past 30 years, would develop and operate the Busang II and Busang III properties, Walsh said.
Freeport Indonesia executive vice-president Paul Murphy, asked to comment on the announcement, said: "The Bre-X press release speaks for itself and we await the government response."

The Mines and Energy Ministry said the minister, Ida Bagus Sudjana, would hold a news conference on Tuesday at 10 a.m. (0300 GMT). Sources close to the negotiations said Bre-X had submitted its latest proposal to the ministry.
"This is a great day for both Bre-X shareholders and for the people of Indonesia," Walsh said.
Bre-X said in a separate statement that further tests at Busang had increased the calculated gold reserves by 13.6 million ounces to 70.95 million ounces, currently worth over $24 billion.
"We are confident that, as the project drilling and mine construction are finalised, the proven gold reserves will grow substantially," Walsh said.
Bre-X, Freeport McMoRan and Indonesian tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, acting on behalf of Indonesian interests, signed a memorandum of understanding on Busang on Sunday.

Bre-X said its two Indonesian partners in Busang II, which holds the main motherlode, and Busang III, PT Askatindo Karya Mineral and PT Amsya Lyna and their partners, would hold a 30 percent stake and the government 10 percent.
Two state mining companies, tin giant PT Tambang Timah and gold and nickel miner PT Aneka Tambang, have also shown interest in participating.

The Nusamba group, 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto and 10 percent each by Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto, holds a controlling interest of just over 50 percent in Askatindo and Amsya.
There was no mention of the previous front-runner to partner Bre-X, Canada's Barrick Gold Corp, the world's second largest gold miner.

The government last November pressed Bre-X to team up with Barrick, which had an agreement with Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana. It said in December they had agreed to split the find 22.5 percent for Bre-X, 67.5 percent for Barrick and 10 percent for the government.
As other potential partners emerged, the government gave Bre-X and Barrick until Monday (February 17) to settle with their local partners before the Busang development could proceed.
It was no secret that Bre-X was unhappy at the prospect of teaming up with Barrick, whose chief Peter Munk has ambitions to become the world's top gold producer.

Bre-X said Freeport, which industry sources said entered the game only last week, would provide approximately $400 million, or 25 percent of the estimated cost of constructing the Busang mining complex.
"Freeport will also provide up to $1.2 billion in additional funding for the venture through a commitment from a major financial institution.
"The financial strength will allow for the joint venture to proceed without any further dilution to shareholders," it said.
Industry sources said New York's Chase Manhattan Corp would provide the loan, which it was expected to syndicate.
